summary: Replace every occurrence of a literal token.
documentation: replaceAll returns a new string after replacing each non-overlapping occurrence of a search string. A regular expression is also allowed when it has the global flag. String replacement patterns can interpret dollar-sign sequences.
inputs: A search string or global RegExp, and a replacement string or function.
returns: A new string; the original is unchanged.
caution: A non-global RegExp throws. Use a replacement function when replacement text must be treated literally.
scenarios: Render repeated placeholders in a local receipt template.
Normalize a repeated delimiter in a supplier export.
Replace obsolete product labels in a batch of descriptions.
title: Fill a repeated city token
problem: Input is a string. Replace every exact occurrence of {{city}} with Harrisburg. Keep all other characters and case unchanged.
goal: Use String.replaceAll() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use a literal search token so braces do not become regular-expression syntax.
